paper: Local-global crop pairs deleted because 40px patches 'carry insufficient information'; KoLeo replaced by KDE.
code: No official training repository exists (GitHub 404); weights on HF are non-gated MIT and SHA-256 match the local copy.
matters: The deletion is a patch, not an information-boundary mechanism; our three-arm study formalizes exactly the question they sidestepped.

paper: Center-token (mean of 4×4 centered patch tokens) reads out at 0.727 on tile-FM probing while class tokens collapse to 0.52–0.54.
code: Consistent with the released checkpoint layout (12 heads, patch 8).
matters: Justifies token-level (never CLS) targets in any distillation arm.

paper: Env branch encoder described as 'LambdaNet'; MoCo memory queue of 65,536; env-loss weight λ unreported.
code: No LambdaNet — env branch is an independent ResNet-18; queue = 0 (no queue); λ_env = 1.0 via the README command (--env-coef 1.0).
matters: Cite repo values for reproducibility; the paper's reported queue does not exist in code.

paper: Target cell and neighboring cells are masked to prevent shortcut and neighbor-type bias.
code: Hard zeroing in the training loop: patch[0][mask...] = 0, a bool square centered on the nucleus (side = int(size × mask_ratio)); segmentation mode zeroes all nucleus pixels.
matters: Masking happens at the pixel/loss end, after the encoder sees the full image — exactly the family our restricted-teacher arm was designed to test (and it lost).

paper: facebookresearch/iBOT is cited by many; random-MIM described with probability r=0.
code: Official code lives at bytedance/ibot; random-MIM is a ratio list + random.choice (loader.py:37-43), r=0 means full-token distillation; patch target = softmax((logit − center)/τ_p) with centering EMA 0.9, τ_p 0.04→0.07; patch:CLS = 1:1.
matters: r=0 is exactly our winning arm's signal form — the closest mechanism precedent, which is why our claim had to rest on the adaptation-setting attribution, not the signal.

paper: Nuc readout 'samples the feature grid at the registered nuclear center … does not imply a nucleus-restricted receptive field'.
code: Evaluation-only; 304,920 probe runs; protocol scores explicitly not comparable across protocols.
matters: Readout ≠ receptive field: training-signal differences must carry the claim, which shaped our probe contract.

paper: 56µm crop is optimal (FOV sweep 28/56/112/224µm = 79.1/83.3/82.5/77.1 macro-F1); 112µm guard band prevents any test/train view overlap.
matters: Single-task optimum exists but says nothing about two task families preferring different views — our step-0 premise, which failed.

paper: Coordinate query + 2D RoPE cross-attention on a shared tile forward; PCC gains attributed jointly to all components.
code: The paper's own Table 7 admits λ and the Gaussian distance decay 'do not show a clear effect'; CLS global-token fusion consistently degrades (−13.6%).
matters: Do not cite CELLO as evidence that coordinate mechanisms are solved; its working core is the shared tile forward + anchored readout.
